# Task 10: notification mail (real Gmail delivery)

The viewer-access workflow sends two real emails: a notification to **you** (owner) when someone requests access,
and an activation email to the **visitor** after you approve. Nothing is printed to a terminal for you to go and
read: with `ACCESS_NOTIFY_BACKEND=smtp` the message arrives in the Gmail inbox, in the Gmail app on your phone or
desktop.

## 1. Create a Gmail app password (one time, 3 minutes)
1. Google Account > Security > turn on **2-Step Verification**.
2. Google Account > Security > **App passwords** > create one named `TwinGrid`. Google shows 16 characters
   (`abcd efgh ijkl mnop`). Spaces are ignored by TwinGrid.
3. Never commit it. It goes only in `.env` (which must stay untracked) or a secret file (`ACCESS_NOTIFY_SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE`).

## 2. `.env`
```
ACCESS_NOTIFY_BACKEND=smtp
ACCESS_NOTIFY_SMTP_USER=yourname@gmail.com
ACCESS_NOTIFY_SMTP_PASSWORD=abcdefghijklmnop
ACCESS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5173
```
Host `smtp.gmail.com`, port `587`, STARTTLS, sender and owner address default to the SMTP user. Override with the
variables in `.env.example`.

## 3. Send a real test email (PowerShell, repo root, venv active)
```
python -m src.notify --check          # configuration problems, nothing sent
python -m src.notify                  # real owner-notification test to your own Gmail
python -m src.notify --kind activation --to someoneelse@gmail.com
```
Success prints `ok=True code=ok backend=smtp`. Then open Gmail on your phone: it should be in the inbox (check Spam once).

## 4. Opening links from your phone
The owner email links to `<ACCESS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/admin`. A phone can open `http://localhost:5173` only if the app is
reachable from it. Options: same Wi-Fi with your PC's LAN address (development only), a Cloudflare Tunnel or ngrok
HTTPS URL, or a deployed site. In production the base URL must start with `https://`, otherwise no link email is sent.

## Result codes
`ok`, `not_configured`, `timeout`, `auth_failed`, `refused`, `invalid_recipient`, `error`. Exception text never leaves the adapter.

## What is and is not verified
Tests use a fake local SMTP server (success, auth failure, refused, timeout, bad recipient). **Real Gmail delivery is
verified only when you run `python -m src.notify` with your credentials.** Gmail limits sending to roughly 500 messages
per day for personal accounts; that is ample here.

## Not possible: sending "from the visitor's Gmail"
A server cannot send as the visitor's address without their password (and providers reject spoofed senders). The
visitor submits the form on the site; TwinGrid sends the notification to you from your own account.
